paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Paul writes to a church that, as we'll see, has plenty of trouble, and he starts by telling them who they are. They are "sanctified in Christ Jesus and called to be holy" (1 Corinthians 1:2). Notice he says it before he fixes a single thing. God's call comes first, and then comes the living.

Now look at why Paul can be so thankful. He says the grace was given "in Christ Jesus," and that in Him they have been "enriched in every way" (1 Corinthians 1:4-5). None of it came from the Corinthians being impressive. I have spent years being very much NOT impressive, friend, and God still used me, so I know a gift when I see one.

And here's where it lands for you. Paul says Jesus "will sustain you to the end, so that you will be blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ" (1 Corinthians 1:8). Why can he promise that? Because "God, who has called you into fellowship with His Son Jesus Christ our Lord, is faithful" (1 Corinthians 1:9). So you can wait eagerly, with your ovens warm, because the One who called you is the One who holds you.
